messages:
maria_ng: quick repro for a weird kernel-picker regression on A100s — small head_dim cases (10/12) sometimes pick flashv3 and end up slower when KV cache is on. attaching run details below.

rajiv: can you paste the perf numbers? curious if autotuner mis-ranked candidates or if runtime fallback happened.

maria_ng: yeah watcher showed "picked=flashv3" then a fallback to sdpa slow path a few steps later. ran with kv_cache=true, causal=true.

# profiler snippet (from local repro):
```
profiler: model=redwood-7b, seq=1024, head_dim=12, heads=64
kernel_picker: candidates=[flashv2, flashv3, sdpa]
initial_pick=flashv3
observed_latency_ms: step1=48.2 step2=52.7 -> fallback to sdpa
baseline_sdpa=19.1
baseline_flashv2=20.0
env: A100-40GB, cuda=12.2, cudnn=8.4
kv_cache=true, kv_stride=384, microbatch=1
seqlen_profile=bimodal(prefix=800, response=64)
```

rajiv: woah sdpa that much faster? that suggests our cost model is overestimating flashv3 for head_dim=12. do we cache any kernel timing per (head_dim, seqlen, causal)?

derek_s: autotuner keeps a per-(arch, hd, seqlen_bucket, causal) table, but we use the first few probes as priors. if kv_cache is enabled, effective seqlen walk causes memory patterns that change kernel perf. looks like probe sampling hit a skewed bucket.

zihao: iirc we have a stride-remap heuristic for head_dim not divisible by 8/16 that forces an "unaligned" codepath in flashv3 which increases register pressure. combined with kv cache scatter (kv_stride not multiple of 128) it trips a slow memory path.

taylor: simple repro idea: run an autotune sweep across head_dim in [8,9,10,12,16,24,32] and seqlen buckets [64,256,512,1024] with kv_cache on/off. we should log raw bandwidth + sm_efficiency counters.

maria_ng: did a quick sweep, attached timings (abbrev): hd=8: flashv3 18ms, hd=12: flashv3 47ms, sdpa 19ms; hd=16 flashv3 17ms. so the spike is isolated to hd 10/12/14 range.

perf-bot: alert: kernel-picker entropy increased for group=(A100,hd=12) over last 6h, variance=+64% vs baseline. linked issue #6421. :warning:

rajiv: sounds like two problems: 1) pick-time cost model not modeling kv_stride-induced memory divergence, 2) flashv3 unaligned register blowup for certain head dims. any quick mitigations?

zihao: short-term mitigation: add a post-pick heuristic — if head_dim % 8 != 0 and kv_cache enabled and seqlen>512, prefer flashv2 or sdpa until we gather more probes. cheap guard.

derek_s: agree. also change probe order to sample candidates with kv_cache enabled earlier (we currently probe without kv_cache first). that'll give realistic timings.

maria_ng: i'll open a small PR for the guard + probe-order change. will also upload the full sweep csv to the issue. planning to roll to canary next week.

taylor: for the long term we should encode kv_stride and cache-line alignment into the cost model and feed in microbenchmarks (bandwidth/warp-occupancy) as features. also consider adding a compact per-card calibration that runs once on install.

rajiv: agreed. priority: PR mitigation -> canary -> collect probes -> refine model. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility.

maria_ng: thanks all, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2891 (wip). I'll post raw logs in #6421.
